headline: Microsoft says it has finished training MAI-Base-2, a 2.8 trillion-parameter AI model it claims needs far less computing power than a leading Chinese rival to reach the same results.
score_reason: Large model announcement from a major company, but efficiency figures are Microsoft's internal tests and the model is not yet released.
importance_line: Businesses that could later license the model gain a possible cheaper option, but the claimed gains come from Microsoft's own tests, post-training is unfinished and release date and price are not announced.
source: Microsoft, as reported by BigGo Finance
summary: Microsoft says on its official blog, as relayed by BigGo Finance, that it has finished pre-training MAI-Base-2, a model with 2.8 trillion parameters, using 16,000 Nvidia GB200 chips over 38 days. The company claims it needs 4.2 to 12.3 times less computing power than DeepSeek's DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base to reach the same performance, based on its internal evaluation; it is still being refined after training, and release timing and pricing are not disclosed.
notes: Investing.com original returned 403; read BigGo Finance relaying Microsoft's blog. BigGo says blog dated the 16th, other outlets report 15 Oct. Efficiency figures are Microsoft's own, not independently verified.
